thread:
Maya P: quick design review request — trace viewer error panel. UX team flagged a few things after the user test: export wording, correlation id prominence, stack trace collapse behavior, and keyboard/accessibility for the trace actions. attaching mock in Figma: https://figma.com/file/xyz

Samir K: saw this. high level: for errors we need the correlation id first (copyable), then a single primary action. multiple secondary actions hidden behind kebab. accessibility: ensure actions have aria-labels and keyboard focus order.

Toni L: +1. specific copy question: should the primary action be "Download error bundle" or "Export trace"? Users in test called it a "bundle" because it included logs + span json. I think "Download error bundle" sets clearer expectations.

Olivia R: from product POV, we need to be consistent with Console naming. We use "Export" elsewhere for small CSVs and "Download" for richer bundles. So "Download error bundle" aligns. Also: how about showing the correlation id as a pill with a copy icon and a copy toast?

Maya P: MVP proposal: header shows: [Severity icon] Error • correlation-id: 1234-abcd [Copy]. Under that, a summary row (timestamp, route, user-id masked). Primary button: "Download error bundle". Secondary (kebab): "Open in log viewer", "Copy trace link", "Export spans (JSON)". Thoughts on ordering?

Samir K: reorder for keyboard users: make "Copy trace link" the first kebab item (hit Enter on kebab -> defaults to first). Also add a keyboard shortcut to copy correlation id: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+C when the trace panel has focus. Add ARIA description explaining what the bundle contains.

Toni L: copy nits: bundle dialog heading could be: "Download error bundle — includes spans, logs, and request headers" (short sentence). For the kebab, use verbs: "Open in Log Viewer", "Copy Trace Link", "Export Spans (JSON)". Small cap differences matter for scanability.

Maya P: accessibility nits from testing: 1) screen reader announced "button" twice for the copy pill. 2) stack traces are long — they should be collapsed by default with a visual affordance to expand to the relevant frame only. 3) keyboard users want Up/Down to move between spans and Enter to expand.

DesignBot: checklist suggestion: - Add aria-live to copy toast - Ensure focus trap when download modal open - Provide skip-to-frames link for screen readers - Implement role="list"/"listitem" for span list

Samir K: performance angle: the trace can have thousands of spans. Virtualize the span list and keep expand/collapse state only for visible items. Also, debounce expand animation to avoid jank.

Toni L: UX microcopy variants for the download modal: Option A title: "Download error bundle" body: "Package includes: spans.json, logs.log, request_headers.json" CTA: "Download". Option B title: "Export trace artifact" body: "Includes spans and raw logs — for debugging and sharing." CTA: "Export". Which reads clearer to an engineer?

Olivia R: prefer Option A — concrete file names reduce ambiguity for support teams. Also add a small line: "This file contains sensitive headers; share only with authorized personnel."

Maya P: on trace drilldown layout — debating side panel vs full-screen modal. Side panel is less disruptive but limited horizontal space for wide stack frames. Full screen allows code copy and syntax highlight. Test feedback: 60% preferred side panel for quick triage, 40% wanted full screen for deep debug. Proposal: default side panel with a "Open full trace" action in kebab.

Samir K: +1. Add a small inline button "Open full trace" that preserves scroll position and selected span. Also expose a deep link with correlation id: /traces/:id?span=:span_id to allow teams to link into specific frames.

Toni L: accessibility keyboard flows I sketched for side panel: - press T to open focused trace (global shortcut) - Tab navigates header → correlation pill → primary CTA → kebab → span list - Up/Down iterate spans - Enter toggles expand - Shift+Enter expand all frames for current span (but default collapsed). I'll add a quick diagram in Figma.

Maya P: copy for the correlation pill tooltip: "Correlation ID — click to copy link to this trace". Is that too long? Alternative: "Copy trace link" as tooltip.

Olivia R: keep tooltip short: "Copy trace link". The pill itself should show a truncated id (first 8 / last 4) with hover showing full. If user hovers, also show a tiny hint: "Press Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+C".

DesignBot: accessibility reminder: tooltip must be accessible (aria-describedby) and not rely only on hover. Provide focusable tooltip target and visible focus ring.

Samir K: small UX detail — stack frame lines should have line numbers and a copy icon that copies the file:line context, not the entire frame. e.g. "app/server.py:201". We can also add a "Copy stack" action that copies the whole visible stack in a human-readable format for support tickets.

Toni L: one more micro-UX: when user clicks "Export Spans (JSON)", show a small ephemeral dropdown to pick time range or all spans. Default preselected: "Visible spans". That avoids accidentally exporting huge payloads.

Maya P: great. next steps I’ll: 1) update Figma with copy and side-panel + modal flows 2) add keyboard nav doc and aria notes 3) handoff a spec for virtualized span list and download modal content. Will @Samir for the ARIA bits.

Olivia R: timeline: try to include this in next patch (release notes: trace UX tweaks). Also add a config flag for Dedicated/Private customers to disable download of headers by default (compliance).

Samir K: noted. tagging infra: need a brief schema for the bundle contents so backend can stream zip parts. Suggested filenames: spans.json, logs.log, request_headers.json, metadata.json

Maya P: thanks everyone — will push updates to the figma link and follow up with a short usability re-test next week. :thumbsup:
